items.title: Effects of different processing methods on the nutritional components and in vitro digestion and fermentation characteristics of foxtail millet (Setaria italica).
items.summary: Foxtail millet (Setaria italica) is highly nutritious but has limited consumer acceptance due to its taste and low nutrient bioavailability. Adopting different processing methods may increase the nutritional components and bioavailability of whole grains. However, no study has systematically compared the different processing methods.

items.title: Germination-driven biochemical remodeling of cereals and pseudocereals: Impacts on nutrient bioaccessibility, phytochemical enrichment, and functional food potential.
items.summary: Global staples include cereal grains (maize, rice, wheat, barley, and sorghum), whose nutritional value is partly limited by antinutritional factors (phytic acid, oxalates, and protease inhibitors) that limit the absorption of minerals and nutrient bioavailability. Germination is an environmentally friendly and effective bioprocess that enhances the nutritional and functional characteristics of cereals by enzymatic, biochemical, and structural changes.

items.title: Excessive Feed Sorting Is Associated With Altered Plasma Metabolism and Distinct Fermentation Responses of Pooled Rumen Microbiota in Dairy Cows.
items.summary: Feed sorting behaviour in dairy cows alters dietary structure and has been associated with rumen dysfunction, but its systemic metabolic consequences and microbial acidogenic potential remain unclear. This study combined in vivo and in vitro approaches to investigate associations between feed sorting behaviour, host metabolism, and rumen microbial fermentation.
items.source_name: Journal of animal physiology and animal nutrition

items.title: Effects of black soldier fly larvae meal on hepatic metabolism and intestinal health in juvenile southern catfish (Silurus meridionalis): Insights from non-targeted metabolomics.
items.summary: To investigate the effects of replacing fishmeal (FM) with black soldier fly larvae meal (BSFLM) on hepatic metabolism and intestinal health in juvenile southern catfish (Silurus meridionalis), six isonitrogenous and isoenergetic diets were formulated with graded replacement levels of 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% and fed to fish for 8 weeks. Intestinal antioxidant parameters, serum immune factors, hepatic free amino acids, and non-targeted hepatic metabolomics were analyzed.
items.source_name: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part D, Genomics & proteomics
